rv.q: The production leaps out of the gate, fast-paced and slick as a sitcom with scant attention paid to Benedick as a soldier having just returned from an unnamed war. The overall tone is instead eagerly hedonistic and full of mocking banter. Sami Fendall’s cool, bright and all-white set is a double-staircase backed by billowy curtains.
While this production has both style and substance, the lack of chemistry between its lovers leaves a sour aftertaste.
Chelsea Walker’s About Nothing offers a pleasant if unremarkable take on one of Shakespeare’s most incisive romantic comedies.
